results.evidence: One route database lists the line as 600 ft, 6 pitches (slab, 5.7 chockstone bypass, 5.0 ramp, then ~2 simul-climbed gully/chimney pitches). A detailed trip report broke the same climb into 4 pitches. No second source confirms 6, and the pitch count depends on how the walking/simul sections are split, so the breakdown's P1-P5 labelling was not changed.

The reader's internal resolution (tree rap at the TOP) is contradicted externally. The route's own database page says the rappels start 30m down and skier's right of the top-out, 4 bolted stations 'and one tree rap down the 5.0 slab at the start' (the route's first pitch is the 5.0 slab). The West Face page describes the original descent as three raps to the notch, the free-hanging chockstone rap, then downclimbing 'or a short 30 foot rap on a tree' to get back on the ground, and the area page says 'one more short rappel' brings you back to the ground. That points to the tree rap being the LAST rappel at the bottom, which would make rappel_detail[0], descent_text and rappel_count_note wrong rather than rope_note/descent/sling_rack. All three statements come from one site, and fixing it means reordering the rappel_detail table, so no patch is written; flagged for a human decision.

The dispute is only in bivy[0].notes, which is owned by the separate camping clean-up; no bivy patch written. Note for that clean-up: the trailhead is just under a mile west of the Washington Pass Overlook (the overlook itself is 0.8 mi east of it), so neither 'half a mile' (bivy) nor '1.5 mi' (waypoint note, approach_variants, trailheadDirection) is exact; see the discovered entry.

Two sources put the climbers' path junction on the Blue Lake Trail at about 1.7 mi (2.7 km) from the trailhead, so the prose's 'about 1.5 miles' is roughly right and the waypoint distMi values (0.6 to the gully base, 1.0 to the summit) are clearly too short. A trip report gives ~5 mi round trip, i.e. ~2.5 mi to the summit, but no second source gives the one-way distance to the gully base or summit, so the waypoint distances were not rewritten.
